parsed_body.theorem_title: The interpolation and analytic bounds exclude fixed admissible data
parsed_body.formal_statement:
theorem OAI.PiExponent.DeterminantContradiction.no_fixed_data_of_interpolation_and_analytic_aggregate
    (hgeometry : GlobalInterpolationStatement) (hanalytic : AnalyticAggregateStatement)
    (nu : ℝ) (hnu : 2 < nu) (d : FixedData nu) : False := by
  sorry
parsed_body.natural_language_statement:
Assume the original global interpolation statement and analytic aggregate statement. For every real exponent $\nu>2$ and every fixed admissible datum $d:\mathrm{FixedData}(\nu)$, these hypotheses imply a contradiction:

$$
\mathrm{GlobalInterpolation}\;\land\;\mathrm{AnalyticAggregate}\;\Longrightarrow\;\bot.
$$

Thus no fixed admissible family can coexist with both source hypotheses at an exponent above $2$.  This is the source theorem that converts the determinant estimates into the conditional lower bound for rational approximations to $\pi$.

parsed_body.theorem_title: The conditional interpolation and analytic determinant argument for pi
parsed_body.formal_statement:
theorem OAI.PiExponent.DeterminantContradiction.piEventualLowerBound_of_interpolation_and_analytic_aggregate
    (hgeometry : GlobalInterpolationStatement) (hanalytic : AnalyticAggregateStatement) :
    PiEventualLowerBound := by
  sorry
parsed_body.natural_language_statement:
Assume the global interpolation statement and the analytic aggregate statement for the original fixed admissible data. Then, for every real $\nu>2$, there is an integer $Q\ge2$ such that every $p\in\mathbb Z$ and $q\in\mathbb N$ with $q\ge Q$ satisfy

$$q^{-\nu}\le\left|\pi-\frac pq\right|.$$

This is the conditional conclusion of the source determinant contradiction, with the original quantified interpolation and analytic hypotheses.
